LanguageData.CBF_S_NewTip: Create a new settlement. It gets town, suburb and countryside.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PickOne: Pick a settlement on the left.
LanguageData.CBF_S_OpenFileTip: Opens the settlement's file in your text editor. The editor reloads changes made there on its own.
LanguageData.CBF_S_FactionOverviewTip: Shows for each faction which settlements it gets and how often.
LanguageData.CBF_S_RerollTip: Recalculates the preview with a new seed.
LanguageData.CBF_S_KindTip: Click switches to the next kind.
LanguageData.CBF_S_ForAll: For all factions of these levels
LanguageData.CBF_S_FactionsTip: Factions or faction categories that explicitly get this settlement.
LanguageData.CBF_S_NoFactionFits: No faction gets this settlement. Pick a tech level with For all factions or add a faction.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MergeTip: Merges the patch files written by the editor into one.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GateWithoutWall: Without a wall there is no gate a gatehouse could fit into. Emplacements still work, the planner puts them on the outline of the town.
LanguageData.CBF_S_UnknownEntry: {0} does not exist. The entry is skipped.
LanguageData.CBF_S_ListGone: The pawn list {0} no longer exists.
LanguageData.CBF_S_FieldNoPlants: A field in {0} has no plants yet.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PenNoAnimals: A pen in {0} has no animals yet.
LanguageData.CBF_S_WeightHint: against other settlements of the same faction
LanguageData.CBF_S_FooterHint: Right-click a tech level to pick it and all higher ones
LanguageData.CBF_S_PreviewWindowTip: Opens the preview large in its own window, with legend and tally.
LanguageData.CBF_S_FarmHousesTip: Which pieces the field is laid around, for example a wind turbine or a mill. Without a choice the planner uses small houses and farmsteads.
LanguageData.CBF_S_CropListTip: Picks a crop list from the Loot tab. The field then draws its plants from it by weight; the individually chosen plants only serve as fallback.
LanguageData.CBF_S_CropListPenTip: Picks a crop list for the pen's growth.
LanguageData.CBF_S_CropListNew: New crop list in the Loot tab
LanguageData.CBF_S_CropListGone: The crop list {0} in {1} does not exist.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GateTip: The gate thing for passages in this ward's wall. Empty takes the standard gate.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DistrictPlacementTip: Where the district is seeded. 0 to 1 each, if all are 0 it is placed at random.
LanguageData.CBF_S_WdStageTip: World Domination tier 1 to 4 this settlement type stands for. A World Domination settlement of this tier prefers it among the types its faction may get. 0 means no tier.
LanguageData.CBF_S_RiafHoldingTip: Makes this settlement type the plan for villages, towns or garrisons of A Rim of Ice and Fire. CBF then builds the houses and walls of such holdings; defenders, levies, residents and stores stay with A Rim of Ice and Fire. A type with a holding kind is not used for normal settlements.
LanguageData.CBF_Lb_ButtonTip: Loot value of the settlement of this type that was built last.
LanguageData.CBF_Lb_NoneYet: Build a settlement of this type first. Its loot is counted while it is built.
LanguageData.CBF_Lb_Note: Market value of everything lying around or stored in containers. Medieval Overhaul lootables that fill only when searched are not included.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MaterialListTip: The material list decides which walls, floors, doors and other things the pieces of this settlement type get.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MaterialListNone: No material list chosen. Without one this settlement type is switched off.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MaterialListUnusable: This material list is unusable, critical roles find no thing.
LanguageData.CBF_S_WdTypeTip: World Domination settlement types this plan stands for, such as mining camp or slave village. Only types of the chosen tier are offered. Empty means any type.
LanguageData.CBF_S_AddWardTip: Add a ward this settlement type does not have yet.
LanguageData.CBF_S_NoWdLootTip: Switches off the extra loot World Domination 2.0 adds to settlements of this type.
LanguageData.CBF_S_IdeoStyleTip: Furniture gets the style of the owning faction's ideoligion.
LanguageData.CBF_S_CampKindsTip: Quest sites this camp plan builds, for example bandit camps, outposts or work sites. Only used for settlements of the kind camp.
LanguageData.CBF_S_IdeoEntryTip: Ideoligion condition: this entry is only built when the faction's ideoligion has, or lacks, the chosen memes or precepts.
LanguageData.CBF_PreviewWardsTip: Colours the old town, suburb and countryside in the preview.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MineTip: A mine dug into the rock from a building of this district: a tunnel with chambers.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MineOreShareTip: Share of rock cells along the mine that become ore, from 0 to 1.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MineHutsTip: Categories of the buildings the mine may start from. Empty: any building of the district.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MineThingsTip: Things placed in the mine. Click to add, remove or move them between chamber, tunnel and entrance.
LanguageData.CBF_S_TreeShareTip: Share of the wild trees inside the settlement that stay standing when it is built, from 0 to 1. 0 clears them all.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MapSizeTip: Edge length of the map this settlement type asks for, 150 to 400. The larger of this and the world setting is used.
LanguageData.CBF_S_CoreSizeTip: Edge length of the settlement core in cells, as a range. The suburb and the countryside grow around it.
